preconditions: this points to a pit_crew_bootstrap container; *this (offset 0x00) holds a valid game-context pointer whose +0x4714 is a writable string buffer and +0x4894 holds the pit index used in PITCREW*%02d / PITDIRECTOR%02d names.
Global dword_8AB6E4 != 2; sub_4A4900 returns without loading when it equals 2.

Content path registry (byte_5EA438 and nullable dword_5EC3D8 / 0x5EC420 / 0x5EC428 path pointers) is initialized so the MAS path fragments (PITANIMS.MAS, TEAM.MAS, PITS.MAS, CDB.MAS, CMAPS.MAS) can be assembled and registered.
postconditions: The container's three children are rebuilt from scratch: this[0x0C] = normal pit-crew MAS loader, this[0x10] = 10-second pit-crew MAS loader, this[0x14] = pit director (only when *this == dword_7C54E8, i.e. the local/player pit).

Each rebuilt child is a mas_loader (24-byte) with +0x0C actor count, +0x10 actor array (120-byte stride, counted header at array-4), +0x14 3D-sound source, populated by parsing ACTOR/DETAIL/MESH/POSITION/MOVE/ROTATE tokens from the MAS file.
Each actor carries a move array at +0x74 (count at +0x70, 28-byte stride); move +0x18 holds the animation index assigned by PitCrewAnimationStringMapper; move +0x0C/+0x10 hold the range start/end.
sub_4A4900 returns the model-load failure flag (non-zero if any resource failed to allocate/load, 0 on a clean load).
side_effects: File I/O: reads the MAS / instance files line-by-line (FileReadUntilNewline, FileCloseWithLock, ConditionalFileHandleCloseWithFlagDispatch); sub_4A51C0 opens and closes an audio/instance stream (AudioStreamOpen + close).
Heap churn: counted-array allocations and frees (OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper / FreeWrapper_7bcf) for actor and move arrays, plus transient 256-byte string buffers.
Content string registry mutations: StringRegistry / StringMatchWithFlagSet on byte_5EA438, with dword_5EC3D8/0x5EC420/0x5EC428 fallback; StringCopyWithBufferRealloc on the shared path buffer.
3D sound source teardown: F_3DSoundSourceDestructor on mas_loader+0x14 when dword_8AFE88 is set (sub_4A29A0).

Render/world queries: RenderCallWithGuard + sub_403640(dword_5EA2C0) camera query, SpatialGridQuery(dbl_7C9360) in sub_4A3B50; global noise-table cursor dword_8AAE70 is advanced on every camera update.

Actor flag propagation: sub_4A3440 sets the actor's bit-12 flag for every actor whose +0x64 is non-zero when container +0x00 bit0 is set; sub_4A3320 forces actor nodes to rotate 180 degrees about Y after load.

Per-frame animation state: sub_4A35F0 / sub_4A3820 recompute each move entry's range proportion via RangeProportionInitializer on a 120-byte actor stride; both share this loop pattern but neither owns the other's data.

Pit-state machine: sub_4A5F20 clears container +0x180, bumps the laps counter at *this+16436+56, calls AIFormationLap(*this) and, when dword_8ACFD4==2, raises the EXITING PITS message (DisqualificationHandler / sub_4BBA90).

lifecycle.owner: sub_4A2980 (mas_loader zero-init + sub_4A3B30 pit-director zero-init; base object constructor sub_4A2220 is out of packet)

sub_4A4900 bootstrap -> sub_4A3220 -> sub_4A2A90 (ACTOR/MOVE parser) -> sub_4A22D0 (per-move loader), sub_4A2770 (wheel mesh load), sub_4A3910 (pit director MAS setup), sub_4A51C0 (instance/tire graphics load)
sub_4A35F0 / sub_4A3820 (per-frame move range update), sub_4A3B50 (pit camera rig -> Vec3CopyToStruct -> ConditionalDispatch), sub_4A3440 (per-actor flag update), sub_4A3FE0 (per-update state reset)
sub_4A4DB0 (container cleanup: frees this[3]/[4]/[5] children) + sub_4A29A0 (array/sound resource cleanup); re-run at the start of every sub_4A4900 reload

Miles audio: F_3DSoundSourceDestructor (mas_loader+0x14 teardown), AudioStreamOpen + stream close in sub_4A51C0

disputes.description: Misleading: body only zeroes this[30]/this[33] and clears a flag bit when this[25] is set — a per-update state reset, not a computation. Name should be treated as heuristic, not evidence of behavior.

Misleading: it is the pit_crew_bootstrap container teardown — frees the three child objects at +0x0C/+0x10/+0x14 via ArrayResourceCleanup/sub_4A3B30 and resets ~30 fields. Nothing in the body touches a UI widget.

Misleading: it reads the render camera but writes a target position/rotation into the pit-director object (via Vec3CopyToStruct on `this`). It is the pit-crew/pit-director animation-camera update, not a general camera routine.
Misleading: it computes per-frame time-fraction buckets from the caller's time value and updates move range proportions. 'Physics channel' is unsupported by the packet's raw C.
Misleading: it is a pit-crew wheel-mesh loader that records two mode bytes (this+0x02, this+0x48) and forwards to PitCrewMeshLoader; the name overstates the dispatch it performs.

unresolved: Scope ambiguity: the packet groups a 25-function SCC and this candidate is one cluster-level contract (kind=lifecycle) with sub_4A4900 as the entry signature. Whether the orchestrator expects one contract per function instead of one cluster contract is not resolvable from the packet alone.

Actor +0x64 (this[25]) is the gate that enables per-move loading in sub_4A22D0, but sub_4A2A90 zeroes it immediately before the base constructor sub_4A2220 runs; the constructor's default for +0x64 is unknown (sub_4A2220 is outside the packet). Without it the MOVE loader appears dead on first pass.

Actor +0x00/+0x02/+0x03 region is a union: DETAIL writes a 16-bit id at +0x00 and a mode byte at +0x02, while the MESH branch writes a mesh filename into the same base via PitCrewMeshLoader/StringCopyWithReverse; the string-buffer width and union layout are unresolved.

sub_4A3320's `this` is a caller stack local (v42, 12 bytes) but the body reads this[5] (+0x14) and writes this[2] (+0x08) beyond that local's bounds — a decompiler artifact; the true object (likely a post-load transform/output struct) is unresolved.

sub_4A4DB0 is invoked as a bare `UIComponentCleanup()` at the head of sub_4A4900; the packet does not prove it is the same `this` object versus a sibling, though the freed offsets (+0x0C/+0x10/+0x14) match this[3]/[4]/[5] exactly.
dbl_7C9360 (SpatialGridQuery argument) is recorded at width 8 from its IDA name only; it may be a pointer to a double. DERIVED, needs the callee signature.
sub_4A24D0's convention: __thiscall-shaped but stateless (single pointer arg in ECX, no `this` use). Its leading sub_589901(lpSrcStr) side effect is unknown.

The exact token strings behind aFrontJackUp .. a10secStarterrel are not visible in the raw C (symbols only), so the PitCrewAnimationStringMapper 0..24 enumeration is exhaustive per the comparison chain but not independently verified against the string index.
Move +0x14 per-instance int array is filled from WideStringComparisonWalkingLinkedList; its semantics (index into an external string list) are unknown without that callee.

sub_4A51C0 is __thiscall with 3 args but called from sub_4A4900 with only 2; the caller passes its own `a2` as the callee's `this`, and `a3` is uninitialized in the call — parameter intent is partially unresolved.
tests_required: Unit: PitCrewAnimationStringMapper maps each of the 24 documented token strings to its distinct index 0..24 and returns 0 for an unmatched string.
Unit: QuoteStrippingCopy strips every ASCII 0x22 byte from the source and returns the sub_589901 result.
Integration: after PitCrewAnimationLoader on a sample MAS, mas_loader+0x0C equals the number of ACTOR records and each actor's +0x70 equals its MOVE record count.
Integration: sub_4A4900 frees and rebuilds this[0x0C]/[0x10]/[0x14] and returns 0 on a clean load, non-zero on any allocation failure.
Regression: sub_4A3910 leaves +0x70 (move count) consistent with +0x74 array length and initializes the first move's range at +0x0C/+0x10.
